name: Harry Stinson
notes: The drummer-who-sings chair — "the archetype's specialist in playing a simple, unbroken two-beat while carrying a harmony part, which is why Marty Stuart's band sounds like a 1960s Bakersfield unit". The window starts in 1990; the Steve Earle Dukes years (1985–87) precede it and are excluded. The drum block is the entry's parameter set, quoted: "deliberate simplicity: straight 8th or 16th snare stream, two-beat kick, hat closed on quarters, backbeat hard and un-gated, fills reduced to accent displacement at 8-bar boundaries — because he is singing a third or fifth above the lead at the same time, the pattern cannot be busy. Model low fill density and near-zero pattern variation across a whole track." So `kick` is a flat 2 on anchors 1 and 3, `velocityTiers.accent` 108–124 for the hard un-gated backbeat, `hihat.base` is "4th" at a 0.026 fill density — the lowest of the stick-kit models here — `percs` is a single ride lane, and the arrangement's `switchUpProb` is 0.02 for "near-zero pattern variation". The song forms are the entry's: "TV-show format implies tight 2:30–3:00 song lengths with cold stop endings", so both structures are short and the outro is two bars. The bass is the stated Superlatives configuration — "bass and steel are the same player, so the bass part and the steel part are conceived together — root–five two-beat under sustained steel pads" — i.e. `rhythm` boom_chick locked to the two-beat kick, with the countermelody carrying the sustained steel. Harmony is placed by his songwriting credits (Ricky Skaggs, Martina McBride, Faith Hill), which "place him inside the mainstream Nashville harmonic vocabulary — I–IV–V and I–V–vi–IV — rather than the bluegrass one". ⚠ The entry states outright that "the drum-pattern parameterisation is inferred from that role and marked [LOW-CONF]", and that flag applies to every drum number above. ⚠ Also INFERRED: `bpm.mode` 140 inside the stated 70–170 band, the scale weights (his entry says keys are n/a for a drummer and only names the harmonic vocabulary), and every melody, countermelody and bassline number. ⚠ **`bassline.rhythm` is `boom_chick` rather than the `mirror_kick` this model overrode its lane with** — the research names the figure outright: *“in the Superlatives configuration bass and steel are the same player (Chris Scruggs), so the bass part and the steel part are conceived together — root–five two-beat under sustained steel pads”*. `boom_chick` is the engine's name for exactly that root–five two-beat, and `country-train`, this model's own lane, already authors it.
